results.title: Generating Major Types of Chinese Classical Poetry in a Uniformed Framework
results.text: We arXiv:2003.11528v1 [cs.CL] 13 Mar 2020 deﬁne a uniﬁed format for formulating all types of training samples by integrating detailed form information, then present a simple form- stressed weighting method in GPT-2 to strengthen the control to the form of the generated poems, with special emphasis on those forms with longer body length.

results.title: Generating Major Types of Chinese Classical Poetry in a Uniformed Framework
results.text: 4.1. Experiment Setup We implement the GPT-2 model based on the transform- ers library (Wolf et al., 2019). The model conﬁguration is 8 attention heads per layer, 8 layers, 512 embedding di- mensions, and 1024 feed-forward layer dimensions. We employ the OpenAIAdam optimizer and train the model with 400,000 steps in total on 4 NVIDIA 1080Ti GPUs.

results.title: Generating Major Types of Chinese Classical Poetry in a Uniformed Framework
results.text: 3.1. Pre-processing We present a uniﬁed format for formulating all types of training samples of SHI and CI by extending the format given in Liao et al. First, we change various punc- tuations between lines into the comma ‘,’, serving as a uni- form separation label between two lines. Second, we utilize three separation labels, [label1] and [label2] to separate be- tween form, title, and body of the poem respectively, and [label3] to separate two stanzas of CI if needed.

results.title: Generating Major Types of Chinese Classical Poetry in a Uniformed Framework
results.text: 4.3. Effect of the Stanza Separation The preliminary observation on the generated poems sug- gests that the inclusion of the stanza separation into the uni- ﬁed format of training samples is beneﬁcial in some degree for meeting the form requirement.
